title: JRE 2274 - Mike Baker
guestBio: Mike Baker is a former CIA covert operations officer and current CEO of Portman Square Group, a global intelligence and security firm. He’s also the host of the "President’s Daily Brief" podcast: a twice daily news report on critical events happening around the globe available on all podcast platforms.

recap:
Joe sits down with Mike Baker, a former CIA covert operations officer who's now running his own intelligence and security firm called Portman Square Group. Baker brings a fascinating perspective on what intelligence work actually looks like versus the Hollywood version everyone thinks they know about.

Baker talks about his background in the CIA and what drove him to leave and start his own operation. The conversation gives you a real inside look at how intelligence agencies actually work, the types of operations they run, and how different that reality is from what you see in movies and TV shows. He's clearly spent decades dealing with serious global threats and has some strong opinions about how the intelligence community operates.

One of the most interesting parts is when they get into current events and how Baker's team stays on top of what's happening around the world through his President's Daily Brief podcast. He breaks down how global security threats are assessed, what actually matters versus what gets sensationalized in the media, and why understanding real intelligence work matters for regular people trying to make sense of world events.

The discussion flows naturally between Baker's personal experiences in the field, his observations about how the intelligence community has changed over time, and his current work helping private clients navigate security issues in an increasingly complex world. Baker comes across as someone who's seen a lot of serious stuff but also maintains perspective about what's actually worth worrying about versus what's just noise.

quotes: The reality of intelligence work is nothing like what you see in the movies.

Running a private intelligence firm means understanding threats that governments sometimes overlook.
The President's Daily Brief keeps people informed about what's actually happening around the world.
